target: A cloud traffic migration has directed links with mandatory minimum flow l(e), maximum capacity u(e), and flow conservation at intermediate services. The team must provide a max-flow-based feasibility certificate that all lower bounds can be honored simultaneously before migration. An ordinary max-flow run that ignores lower bounds is not accepted; the plan must specify the transformation and the exact saturation condition that proves feasibility.
surface: A previous cloud routing plan discarded minimum commitments, assigned every link capacity u(e), ran ordinary source-to-sink max flow, and called the migration feasible whenever total maximum throughput met demand.
structural: An irrigation circulation plan handled channels with lower and upper flow bounds. It first fixed every lower flow and replaced each residual channel capacity by u-l, accumulating the induced net imbalance at every node. It added a super-source and super-sink with demand-balancing arcs (and a sink-to-source arc for an s-t instance), ran max flow, and declared feasibility exactly when every arc leaving the super-source was saturated; it then restored the lower flows.
rubric: Explicitly selects the standard lower-bounded circulation reduction rather than ordinary max flow or an unspecified optimizer.
Fixes lower flows, replaces each edge capacity by u-l, and accumulates node imbalances from lower bounds.
Adds super-source/super-sink balancing arcs and mentions the sink-to-source arc for an s-t instance.
Uses saturation of every super-source outgoing arc (equivalently all demand arcs) as the feasibility certificate, then restores lower flows.
States conservation and 0<=l<=u assumptions or explains that failure to saturate certifies infeasibility.
